node, refused if its simulation reverts, and sent with the estimate plus a
tenth as an explicit limit. A MON spend is checked against the 10 MON reserve
first, and a delegated account is refused a send Monad would revert. The

subject: Run a whole operator's day on the local chain with no MON, the gas sponsored
body:
Privy's gas sponsorship can't run on anvil, so a local build now reproduces
its on-chain shape. With 'A sponsor pays this wallet's gas' ticked on
/localnet:
- the local wallet delegates its address to SponsoredAccount under EIP-7702
  and signs each call;
- /api/localnet/sponsor sends the call from a sponsor key (anvil #9),
  scoped to Thenar's contracts and the local USDC;
- the protocol sees the operator's own address and pays it;
- the faucet sends USDC only, and the gas warnings stand down.

SponsoredAccount (deployed by localnet.mjs at its CREATE2 address) accepts
a call only with the address's own signature over chain, nonce, target,
value and data, so the sponsor cannot alter or replay what it delivers.

It also answers EIP-1271. The first run without it showed why it matters:
once an address carries delegated code, the x402 facilitator verifies its
USDC authorisation through isValidSignature, and the purchase was refused
(invalid_exact_evm_signature). Privy's delegate accounts answer EIP-1271,
and a stand-in that didn't would have hidden that dependency.

SPONSORED=1 test/live-localnet.mjs (npm run test:localnet:sponsored) passes:
- a 0-MON operator registers its passkey, runs, and is paid exactly the run's
  payout while the sponsor pays the gas;
- it buys the corpus over x402 from its delegated address.
The unsponsored journey still passes. Foundry covers the account (7 tests).

subject: Audit the corpus against its commitment from a Chainlink DON
body:
cre/corpus-audit is a CRE workflow. On a cron, every node fetches the
episode hashes Thenar would sell (/api/corpus/episodes, new), builds each
task's Merkle root itself, and the nodes agree on the roots. The DON reads
the verifier's commitments from CorpusManifest on monad-testnet in one
Multicall3 call, gives each task a verdict (Matches, Grown, Short, Altered
or Uncommitted), and writes the report to CorpusAudit, a ReceiverTemplate
that accepts it only from the KeystoneForwarder and keeps the newest verdict
per task.

Checked without a DON: Foundry tests for the receiver; test/live-cre-audit.mjs
on the local chain (the workflow's roots equal lib/merkle.ts's and the
manifest route's, verdicts follow real commitments, and a deployed receiver
stores the exact report the workflow encodes); and the workflow compiles to
WASM. Simulating it against Monad needs `cre login`, which is the user's.

Chainlink's IReceiver and ReceiverTemplate are copied from the CRE docs;
Ownable is a minimal stand-in for OpenZeppelin's. The app's typecheck, lint
and deploy uploads leave cre/ out.

verifies its signed command with the arm relay's own check, derives it
again with nothing stored in the browser, buys the task's corpus over x402
from /corpus and matches the file to its SalesLog entry, and reads the run
and the sale back from the indexer on /leaderboard. Anvil keeps only 300
states in memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Let the buyer agent run on Kimi
body:
AGENT_LLM=kimi runs the same corpus-buying loop on Moonshot's kimi-k2.6
(KIMI_MODEL to change it, MOONSHOT_API_KEY required). Its reasoning is sent
back on each assistant turn as Kimi asks, and its temperature is left to the
model. The turn kept in the history now holds only the tool call that was
answered: a turn with two calls kept both while answering one, which a
strict endpoint refuses.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Read the Envio indexer's history onto /leaderboard
body:
Monad's RPC serves logs 100 blocks at a time, so the app could not show
history it does not keep itself. /api/indexer reads the HyperIndex
indexer's aggregates (Stats, DailyStat, the most recent Operators) from
ENVIO_GRAPHQL_URL, server side, and /leaderboard draws them: totals, two
weeks of runs day by day, and who ran last. A deployment without an indexer
shows nothing rather than zeros it never read.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Buy one task's corpus from /corpus over x402, with your own wallet
body:
The per-pull x402 sale was only reachable by an agent with a key in a
script. /corpus?task=N now makes the same purchase from the page: the
operator's wallet (the embedded one Privy made) signs the one-cent USDC
authorisation, the facilitator settles it and pays the gas, the file
downloads, and the page shows the settlement, the file's SHA-256 and its
SalesLog entry. Privy's useX402Fetch speaks x402 v1 and the paywall is v2,
so the payment is made with x402's own v2 client over the wagmi wallet.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Let Privy pay operators' gas, behind NEXT_PUBLIC_PRIVY_GAS_SPONSORSHIP
body:
An operator who signs in with email has an embedded wallet with no MON, and
had to find some before the first paid run. With sponsorship enabled for
Monad Testnet in the Privy dashboard and the flag set, the passkey
registration, every submit and every other write from the shared write path
go through Privy's sendTransaction with sponsor: true. A wallet the operator
brought still pays for itself through wagmi. The hook is chosen at build
time, so a local-chain build never calls Privy.

The gas warnings stand down for a sponsored wallet, and /api/submitted no
longer requires the transaction to be addressed to the protocol: a sponsored
run reaches it through the operator's delegated account. The protocol's own
TrajectoryAccepted log for the run is what it checks, as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Show the keys one passkey makes, and prove the SO-101 one on /passkey
body:
The passkey's PRF already made the Ed25519 key the arm relay requires, but
nothing on screen showed it, so it could only be seen with a physical arm.
/passkey now lists the identity key and the SO-101 key with the salt each
comes from, derives the SO-101 key on demand, signs a command the way the
station does, verifies it in the page with the public key alone, and ends
the session. The same passkey on another device shows the same key.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

subject: Check Thenar against every Metropolis sponsor bounty
body:
docs/SPONSOR-GAP.md: the submission branch (main; monad is fully
contained, quest-teleop is the superseded prototype, kept on its own
branches), the track (T4, and why Xorv being T4 too matters), and per
bounty what Thenar does, the gap against the bounty's own wording,
effort, value and the plan, plus what only the user can do.

subject: Keep the hero's words off the film
body:
The film started a fixed 38% down the screen, so on a short or narrow
screen it slid up behind the subtitle and 'See what we build', which
read as grey on a bright glass arm. It now sits in the page flow under
the buttons, fading in at its top edge, with the logo strip tucked into
its faded bottom. 'See what we build' is a glass button with white text,
and 'Open the app' in the nav stays on one line on a phone.
